You translate questions about a Swiss clinical knowledge graph (SPHN schema, Virtuoso 7.2 triple store) into one SPARQL SELECT query.

DATA LAYOUT
- Every patient is one named graph: patient data must be matched inside GRAPH ?g { ... }. A patient is ?g, so "number of patients" is COUNT(DISTINCT ?g).
- Terminologies (ICD-10-GM, CHOP, SNOMED CT, LOINC, UCUM, ...) with labels and hierarchies live in GRAPH <https://biomedit.ch/rdf/sphn-resource/global> (rdfs:label, rdfs:subClassOf).
- Coded values: a record links a code node with a predicate such as sphn:hasCode; the code node is typed with a terminology class. Write `?code isa icd-10-gm:E11` to mean "this code or any sub-code" (this expands to rdf:type with RDFS inference). Use isa for every fixed ICD-10-GM, CHOP, SNOMED CT, LOINC or ORDO code. ICD-10-GM and CHOP nodes are stored with versioned classes, so a fixed ICD/CHOP code without isa matches nothing. Several alternative codes: `{ ?code isa icd-10-gm:E10 } UNION { ?code isa icd-10-gm:E11 }` (never VALUES with `?code a ?cls` for ICD/CHOP).
- To report which code a record has: `?code a ?concept . FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?concept), STR(icd-10-gm:)))` (the same node can also carry classes of other systems).
- Quantities: `?x sphn:hasQuantity ?q . ?q sphn:hasValue ?value ; sphn:hasUnit/sphn:hasCode ?unit . ?unit a ucum:kg .` Check the unit whenever values are compared, averaged or banded (ages use years ucum:a, months, days...).
- Administrative sex: `?sex_record a sphn:AdministrativeSex ; sphn:hasCode ?sex_code . ?sex_code a ?sex_concept .` with VALUES (?sex_concept ?sex) { (snomed:248153007 "male") (snomed:248152002 "female") (snomed:32570681000036106 "indeterminate") }.
- Named individuals of sphn-individual: are plain IRIs, e.g. `?dx sphn:hasRank sphn-individual:Principal`.
- Dates are xsd:dateTime. Durations: bif:datediff("day"|"hour"|"minute", ?start, ?end). YEAR(), MONTH() also work.
- Use only the classes and predicates listed in the schema below; they are the ones present in the data.

QUERY RULES
- Answer with aggregates (counts, averages, shares) unless the question explicitly asks for something else.
- Every triple pattern must connect to the others through shared variables; records from different patterns of the same patient are joined on ?g only when the question relates them per patient.
- Do not multiply counts: when two independent record sets of the same patient are joined, count with DISTINCT or aggregate per patient in a subquery first.
- "Patients with A" -> COUNT(DISTINCT ?g). "Records/events" -> COUNT(DISTINCT ?record).
- Optional per-patient flags: OPTIONAL { GRAPH ?g { ... } BIND(?g AS ?flag_patient) } then COUNT(DISTINCT ?flag_patient).
- All patients (denominators, "patients without X"): anchor with GRAPH ?g { ?patient a sphn:SubjectPseudoIdentifier }. "Without / never" -> that anchor plus FILTER NOT EXISTS { GRAPH ?g { ... } }.
- Labels of codes are in the terminology graph: `?code a ?concept .` inside GRAPH ?g, then GRAPH <https://biomedit.ch/rdf/sphn-resource/global> { ?concept rdfs:label ?label }.
- Percentages: ROUND(1000.0 * part / total) / 10.
- First/earliest event per patient: aggregate MIN(...) in a subquery grouped by ?g.
- Virtuoso: REPLACE() needs a pattern that cannot match the empty string; use STRAFTER(STR(?iri), "#") for local names of sphn IRIs.
- Do not write PREFIX declarations: all prefixes (sphn, sphn-individual, snomed, icd-10-gm, chop, loinc, ucum, geno, so, obi, efo, edam, ordo, rdf, rdfs, xsd, bif) are added automatically.

QUESTION: Ich arbeite derzeit an einem Audit zur Datenqualität unserer elektronischen Patientenakten und muss verstehen, wie häufig spezifische ICD-10-CM-Codes im gesamten System vorkommen, ohne mich auf bestimmte Diagnosegruppen oder Patientensegmente zu beschränken. Könnten Sie mir bitte eine vollständige Aufschlüsselung geben, die zählt, wie oft jeder einzelne Code-Eintrag in allen vorhandenen Datensätzen verwendet wird? Ich benötige diese allgemeine Häufigkeitsverteilung aller kodierten Eigenschaften, um systemweite Muster zu identifizieren.

```sparql
SELECT ?p (COUNT(*) AS ?uses) WHERE { GRAPH ?g { ?s ?p ?o } } GROUP BY ?p ORDER BY DESC(?uses)
```

QUESTION: What's the list of the 5 most common medical device codes, sorted by patient count?

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?code (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?device rdf:type sphn:MedicalDevice .
    ?device sphn:hasTypeCode ?device_code .
    ?device_code rdf:type ?code .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?code
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
LIMIT 5
```

QUESTION: List the number of patients with a documented exposure to Rickettsia australis antibody for each administrative sex.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?sex (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?exp rdf:type sphn:Exposure .
    ?exp sphn:hasAgentCode ?exp_code .
    ?exp_code isa <http://snomed.info/id/444425009> .
    ?admin_sex rdf:type sphn:AdministrativeSex .
    ?admin_sex sphn:hasCode ?sex_code .
    ?sex_code rdf:type ?sex .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?sex
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
```

```sparql
}
```
```sparql
GROUP BY ?sex
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
```

- Coded values: a record links a code node with a predicate such as sphn:hasCode; the code node is typed with a terminology class. Write `?code isa icd-10-gm:E11` to mean "this code or any sub-code" (this expands to rdf:type with RDFS inference). Use isa for every fixed ICD-10-GM, CHOP, SNOMED CT, LOINC or ORDO code. ICD-10-GM and CHOP nodes are stored with versioned classes, so a fixed ICD/CHOP code without isa matches nothing. Several alternative codes: `{ ?code isa icd-10-gm:E10 } UNION { ?code isa icd-10-gm:E11 }` (never VALUES with `?code a ?cls` for ICD/CHOP).

- Coded values: a record links a code node with a predicate such as sphn:hasCode; the code node is typed with a terminology class. Write `?code isa icd-10-gm:E11` to mean "this code or any sub-code" (this expands to rdf:type with RDFS inference). Use isa for every fixed ICD-10-GM, CHOP, SNOMED CT, LOINC or ORDO code. ICD-10-GM and CHOP nodes are stored with versioned classes, so a fixed ICD/CHOP code without isa matches nothing. Several alternative codes: `{ ?code isa icd-10-gm:E10 } UNION { ?code isa icd-10-gm:E11 }` (never VALUES with `?code a ?cls` for ICD/CHOP).

- Quantities: `?x sphn:hasQuantity ?q . ?q sphn:hasValue ?value ; sphn:hasUnit/sphn:hasCode ?unit . ?unit a ucum:kg .` Check the unit whenever values are compared, averaged or banded (ages use years ucum:a, months, days...).

- Dates are xsd:dateTime. Durations: bif:datediff("day"|"hour"|"minute", ?start, ?end). YEAR(), MONTH() also work.
- Use only the classes and predicates listed in the schema below; they are the ones present in the data.

- Answer with aggregates (counts, averages, shares) unless the question explicitly asks for something else.
- Every triple pattern must connect to the others through shared variables; records from different patterns of the same patient are joined on ?g only when the question relates them per patient.

QUESTION: List the lab test codes seen in the most patients—top 10 with count.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?code (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?test rdf:type sphn:LabTest .
    ?test sphn:hasCode ?test_code .
    ?test_code rdf:type ?code .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?code
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
LIMIT 10
```

QUESTION: What is the annual count of patients diagnosed with an oncology diagnosis of ICD-10 code H40.9 (Glaukom, nicht näher bezeichnet)?

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?year (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?onco rdf:type sphn:OncologyDiagnosis .
    ?onco sphn:hasCode ?onco_code .
    ?onco_code rdf:type icd-10-gm:H40.9 .
    ?onco sphn:hasIncidenceDateTime ?onco_date .
  }
  BIND(YEAR(?onco_date) AS ?year)
}
GROUP BY ?year
ORDER BY ?year
```

QUESTION: How many patients have each death record code, and which 5 are most common?

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?code (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?death rdf:type sphn:Death .
    ?death sphn:hasConditionCode ?death_code .
    ?death_code rdf:type ?code .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?code
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
LIMIT 5
```

QUESTION: Which imaging procedure codes show up most often? Return the top 20 with patient frequencies.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?code (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?img rdf:type sphn:ImagingProcedure .
    ?img sphn:hasCode ?img_code .
    ?img_code rdf:type ?code .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?code
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
LIMIT 20
```

QUESTION: How many patients per top 5 lab test code? Break it down.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?code (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?test rdf:type sphn:LabTest .
    ?test sphn:hasCode ?test_code .
    ?test_code rdf:type ?code .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?code
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
LIMIT 5
```

QUESTION: How many patients showed a sample of type 'Leukocyte specimen from patient' each year?

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?year (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {

    ?sample sphn:hasMaterialTypeCode ?sample_code .
    ?sample_code isa snomed:122584003 .
    ?sample sphn:hasCollectionDateTime ?sample_date .
  }
  BIND(YEAR(?sample_date) AS ?year)
}
GROUP BY ?year
ORDER BY ?year
```

- Coded values: a record links a code node with a predicate such as sphn:hasCode; the code node is typed with a terminology class. Write `?code isa icd-10-gm:E11` to mean "this code or any sub-code" (this expands to rdf:type with RDFS inference). Use isa for every fixed ICD-10-GM, CHOP, SNOMED CT, LOINC or ORDO code. ICD-10-GM and CHOP nodes are stored with versioned classes, so a fixed ICD/CHOP code without isa matches nothing. Several alternative codes: `{ ?code isa icd-10-gm:E10 } UNION { ?code isa icd-10-gm:E11 }` (never VALUES with `?code a ?cls` for ICD/CHOP).

- Use only the classes and predicates listed in the schema below; they are the ones present in the data.

- Answer with aggregates (counts, averages, shares) unless the question explicitly asks for something else.

QUESTION: Fetch the raw data for a billed procedure 'Detail der Subkategorie 99.10'.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?proc_date ?code_class
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?proc rdf:type sphn:BilledProcedure .
    ?proc sphn:hasCode ?proc_code .
    ?proc_code isa chop:99.10.0 .
    ?proc sphn:hasRank sphn-individual:Principal .
    ?proc sphn:hasStartDateTime ?proc_date .
    ?proc_code rdf:type ?code_class .
  }
}
LIMIT 100
```

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"

  GRAPH ?g {
```

```sparql
    ?proc sphn:hasStartDateTime ?proc_date .
  }
  BIND(YEAR(?proc_date) AS ?year)
}
GROUP BY ?year
ORDER BY ?year
```

QUESTION: Tell me the year-by-year count of patients with an allergy episode manifesting as Injury in water transport caused by engine room machinery, occupant on small unpowered boat injured.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?year (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?allergy rdf:type sphn:AllergyEpisode .
    ?allergy sphn:hasManifestationCode ?allergy_code .
    ?allergy_code isa snomed:215698009 .
    ?allergy sphn:hasDateTime ?allergy_date .
  }
  BIND(YEAR(?allergy_date) AS ?year)
}
GROUP BY ?year
ORDER BY ?year
```

QUESTION: Quick one - does patient 1058553 have a billed procedure 'Detail der Subkategorie 79.36'?

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?year (COUNT(*) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH <http://example.org/graph/gen_mock_data-1_1058553> {
    ?proc rdf:type sphn:BilledProcedure .
    ?proc sphn:hasCode ?proc_code .
    ?proc_code isa chop:79.36.0 .
    ?proc sphn:hasStartDateTime ?proc_date .
  }
  BIND(YEAR(?proc_date) AS ?year)
}
GROUP BY ?year
ORDER BY ?year
```

```sparql
  }
  BIND(YEAR(?img_date) AS ?year)
}
GROUP BY ?year
ORDER BY ?year
```

- Coded values: a record links a code node with a predicate such as sphn:hasCode; the code node is typed with a terminology class. Write `?code isa icd-10-gm:E11` to mean "this code or any sub-code" (this expands to rdf:type with RDFS inference). Use isa for every fixed ICD-10-GM, CHOP, SNOMED CT, LOINC or ORDO code. ICD-10-GM and CHOP nodes are stored with versioned classes, so a fixed ICD/CHOP code without isa matches nothing. Several alternative codes: `{ ?code isa icd-10-gm:E10 } UNION { ?code isa icd-10-gm:E11 }` (never VALUES with `?code a ?cls` for ICD/CHOP).

- Dates are xsd:dateTime. Durations: bif:datediff("day"|"hour"|"minute", ?start, ?end). YEAR(), MONTH() also work.
- Use only the classes and predicates listed in the schema below; they are the ones present in the data.

QUESTION: Review patient ID-1054500's file for an allergy episode manifesting as Oxazepam overdose.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?year (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?allergy sphn:hasSubjectPseudoIdentifier ?subject .
?subject sphn:hasIdentifier "1054500" .
?allergy rdf:type sphn:AllergyEpisode .
    ?allergy sphn:hasManifestationCode ?allergy_code .
    ?allergy_code isa snomed:296106004 .
    ?allergy sphn:hasDateTime ?allergy_date .
  }
  BIND(YEAR(?allergy_date) AS ?year)
}
GROUP BY ?year
ORDER BY ?year
```

```sparql
}
```

QUESTION: Provide a ranked list of the top 10 medical device codes along with the number of associated patients for each.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?code (COUNT(DISTINCT ?g) AS ?patients)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?device rdf:type sphn:MedicalDevice .
    ?device sphn:hasTypeCode ?device_code .
    ?device_code rdf:type ?code .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?code
ORDER BY DESC(?patients)
LIMIT 10
```

```sparql
}
```

```sparql
ORDER BY ?proc_date
```

QUESTION: Fetch one patient where a documented exposure to Chlormadinone acetate and an identified organism Toxocara cati apply.

```sparql
DEFINE sql:select-option "order"
SELECT ?g (COUNT(DISTINCT ?exp) AS ?records)
WHERE {
  GRAPH ?g {
    ?exp rdf:type sphn:Exposure .
    ?exp sphn:hasAgentCode ?exp_code .
    ?exp_code isa <http://snomed.info/id/734647009> .
    ?org rdf:type sphn:Organism .
    ?org sphn:hasCode ?org_code .
    ?org_code isa snomed:36283001 .
  }
}
GROUP BY ?g
ORDER BY DESC(?records)
```
